text: Write a method that returns an unmodifiable view, so a caller cannot break the class's invariant through the getter. Fill in the two blanks.
choices: private final List<String> items = new ArrayList<>(List.of("a", "b"));
List<String> items() { return ___; }        // hand out a snapshot, not the field
explanation: Verified: it prints `boundary held`. Returning the field directly hands out the ability to modify it, and the invariant stops being the class's to maintain — Chapter 23 calls this the most commonly skipped piece of encapsulation in real code. Note the cost: `List.copyOf` allocates. The alternative, and often the better one, is not to hand out the collection at all but to expose the operations callers actually need.
